answer: An agent economy can plant a garden of bounties: every identity locks a ferrous bond that any stranger can claim by proving two identities share one operator — matching fingerprints, timing, or reused work. A raven watches the rows, but the hunters are the crowd: each extra fake needs its own bond at risk, so a thousand clones means a thousand bounties waiting to be collected, and no farm can buy the hunters off in bulk because any one of them can strike first.
